To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ribavirin is an effective therapy of hepatitis C, but it is not curative, and that combination therapy of ribaviron with α interferon improves the sustained response rates compared with α interferon given alone.

ribavirin in standard oral doses combined with α‐interferon in standard intramuscular doses for 6 months is superior to interferon alone for achieving sustained virologic and biochemical responses in patients who have failed to respond to α interferen.
combination therapy is superior in achieving sustained virological and biochemical responses in patients who do not have a sustained response to interferon alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antiviral agents and with the optimization of the use of currently available agents.
the development of a new antiviral drug, which is a nucleosidic analogue of 5‐fluorouracil (5FU) with a high activity against the hepatitis C virus.
the development of a therapy for chronic hepatitis C, which is based on the combination of ribavirin and interferon‐alfa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of ribavirin and α interferon is a new standard of therapy for patients who are not responding to α interferon.

the combination of interferon‐ribavirin has been shown to be more effective than interferon alone, and ribavirin alone, but that further studies are required to determine the optimal duration of therapy.
combination therapy of ribavirins and interferons has been shown to be more effective than monotherapy with interferon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of ribavirin and interferon is superior to interferon alone in patients with chronic hepatitis C.
the combination of α interferon and ribavirus is the standard of care for the treatment of patients infected with hepatitis C virus.
the combination of interferon and ribavirusin is the most efficacious and tolerable treatment for patients with chronic hepatitis C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ribavirin and α‐IFN in combination is a very effective therapy for patients with HCV infection.
ribavirin, when used as monotherapy or in combination with interferon, has a limited role as a therapy of hepatitis C.
combination therapy with interferon and ribaviron is superior to interferon alone, but only in patients with an unfavorable profile for interferon response.
